qualifications: Deliverables 3 (XLSX workbook) and 4 (PDF/native memorandum) could not be produced: this control has no file-generation tools. Nothing was created, exported or delivered as a file. See 'blocked'.

Source access: analysis relies solely on the supplied PDF text extractions and XLSX cell coordinates. There is no image or OCR access, so any content conveyed only graphically (charts, stamps, signatures, scanned exhibits) could not be reviewed. No source in this packet was flagged as containing no extractable text.

Three income bases are deliberately kept separate and are NOT interchangeable: (a) historical T12 Sep-2025-Aug-2026 (EGI 866,400; NOI before reserves 602,400; NCF 590,880); (b) point-in-time contractual rent at 2026-08-31 ($60,000/month = $720,000 annualized base rent, before other income); (c) the supplied underwriting scenario (EGI 921,000; NOI before reserves 629,760; NCF 625,440).

Reconciliation - gross potential rent: rent roll annualized GPR is $720,000; T12 GPR is $759,600; the underwriting plan uses $780,000. The plan states its GPR is a supplied scenario, not inferred from the T12, and that historical income should not be forced to equal an annualized rent roll. The $60,000 gap between plan GPR and T12 GPR, and the $60,000 gap between T12 GPR and annualized contractual rent, are unexplained by the packet. Achieving $780,000 implicitly requires leasing suite 110 (1,600 SF; market $3,400/month = $40,800/year) and/or rent growth not evidenced by any executed lease. This is the single largest driver of the sizing outcome and should be a condition of credit review.

Reconciliation - T12 arithmetic: all monthly columns on T12-Statement.pdf pp.1-2 foot to the printed Annual column for every line item (GPR, vacancy, concessions, bad debt, other income, all seven expense lines, reserves, capex, P&I, depreciation). No unexplained variances.

The T12 statement prints no NOI/NCF subtotals; NOI before reserves and NCF after reserves shown here are derived. Per Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1, any accounting-package label of after-reserve cash flow as 'property NOI' is preserved as reported but is separately identified here. Replacement reserves ($11,520), capital improvements ($74,000), loan P&I ($294,000) and depreciation ($180,000) are excluded from operating expenses.

Reserves basis differs materially between periods: T12 actual $11,520 (~$0.40/SF) versus underwritten $4,320 ($0.15/SF per plan). Underwriting at the lower reserve raises NCF by $7,200 and therefore raises the DSCR-constrained loan by roughly $72,000. Flagged because DSCR is the binding constraint.
Management fee: T12 actual $18,000 is only 2.08% of T12 EGI. The lender-normalized fee of $36,840 (4.00% of underwritten EGI) is $18,840 higher and reduces underwritten NOI accordingly.

Value of $10,076,160 is an indicative capitalization result only (underwritten NOI before reserves / 6.25%). Lender-Terms.pdf p.1 expressly states no appraisal is implied. No appraisal, environmental report, market comparables, sponsor track record or credit approval is supplied; no market, sponsor or lender opinions are asserted here.

Sizing was performed on unrounded intermediates per Lender-Terms.pdf p.1; displayed dollars are rounded for readability. The lender may round the final commitment down (e.g., to the nearest $1,000 = $6,261,000), which would slightly increase DSCR/debt yield and reduce cash out by about $945.

Because the contract rate (6.35%) equals the sizing floor and the interest-only period is 0 months, first-year contractual debt service equals sizing debt service ($500,352). There is no IO benefit and no rate-step benefit; if the contract rate were later set above 6.35%, the sizing rate would follow it upward per the term sheet.

The deal sizes to the DSCR minimum exactly (1.2500x) with only ~$35,663 of LTV headroom, i.e. it is effectively dual-constrained. Any reduction in underwritten NCF, or any increase in the sizing rate, reduces proceeds roughly dollar-for-dollar with no cushion.

Tenant/lease notes: 9 of 10 suites occupied (94.44% by area). Suite 106 (Tenant F LLC, 3,300 SF, $7,400/month = $88,800/year, 11.5% of rent roll) expires 2027-08-31, inside the 60-month loan term; suites 102 and 107 expire 2028-08-31. Rollover of these three suites totals $88,800 + $48,000 + $103,200 = $240,000/year (40% of contractual base rent) before maturity. No renewal probabilities, TI/LC allowances or downtime assumptions are supplied in the packet, so re-tenanting cost is unquantified.

Suite 110 vacant market rent ($3,400/month) is context only and is excluded from contractual income per Rent-Roll.xlsx C19. The suite 101 security deposit ($6,000) is a liability, not income, per Lease-File.pdf sec.4.

Unresolved evidence items: (1) primary insurer renewal certificate behind the $34,800 premium; (2) the interest-rate swap confirmation and its termination economics; (3) support for the $780,000 underwritten GPR; (4) the $0 one-time casualty-cleanup add-back cited in the plan for R&M (stated as $0, so no adjustment was made); (5) reason for the reserve-per-SF change; (6) any lease documents for suites 102-110 (only the suite 101 lease was supplied, so all other rents rely on the rent roll alone).

This is internal-review underwriting analysis, not a legal opinion, appraisal, or credit commitment. All parties, addresses and figures are fictional evaluation material; no external data, geocoding, comps or contacts were used.
